Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (in force since 1 January 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), arts. 305bis and 305ter; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Financial Sector (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0; Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance for Financial Intermediaries (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.01; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), arts. 697i et seq. as amended by the Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and Trusts; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411) and Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411.11); Federal Act on Economic Sanctions (Embargo Act), SR 946.231, with implementing SECO sanctions ordinances

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Deed of incorporation and articles of association of the Swiss stock company (Aktiengesellschaft / Société anonyme)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public in the canton of registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for certified copies used abroad; original public deed is notarized domestically under Swiss law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / commercial register excerpt for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for apostille states; Swiss consular legalization for non-apostille states, followed by certified translation into German, French or Italian

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each beneficial owner, director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national civil registry / passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy by a recognized notary or consular officer; apostille or consular legalization where the commercial register or financial intermediary requires evidentiary-grade document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for formation of the Swiss AG, including authority to sign the notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary or notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization depending on origin country, with certified translation into the language of the registers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all direct shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and every individual ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% against the Swiss SECO sanctions ordinances, UN Security Council consolidated list, US OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list and UK HMT consolidated list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, high-risk countries, opaque ownership chains and NVOCC payment flows. The Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office and AMLA reporting duties apply, and the due diligence file must be available to FINMA, MROS and the commercial register before notarial execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt); filings are made through the Swiss Federal Commercial Register iHandelsregister platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be written in the Latin alphabet and expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh in the relevant canton). The corporate law form indicator must be added using the official language of the registered office: Aktiengesellschaft/AG, Société anonyme/SA or Società anonima/SA. Foreign names must be transliterated and must not mislead the public or conflict with Swiss public order, business truth and deceptive-name rules under articles 944 et seq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canton or municipal names creating official-state association
Red Cross, Army, University, police or reserved governmental indicators
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed by written request to the Cantonal Commercial Register within the reservation period, at the registry's discretion for a further period not exceeding 180 days. If the name is rejected, the registry issues a written refusal with reasons. The applicant may file an administrative objection with the Cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority within 30 days of notification, then appeal to the Cantonal Administrative Court and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court on federal-law grounds. A corrected name application may be re-filed before expiry of the reservation window or after payment of a new reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, mail-only address or letter-box arrangement is not permissible for a Swiss AG. The registered office must be a real, accessible address in the canton capable of receiving service of process, maintaining corporate records and demonstrating local commercial substance. A licensed fiduciary administration office may serve as registered office only if the company genuinely carries on management, bookkeeping and record-keeping functions at that location. For an NVOCC ocean freight forwarding business, the authority will expect documentary substance such as bills of lading, contracts, customs records and operational files.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% annual likelihood for a newly incorporated NVOCC company using a licensed fiduciary registered office without dedicated local premises; below 5% where the company maintains its own physical office, staff, payroll and books. Swiss tax, social insurance, customs and AML authorities may conduct unannounced on-site inspections and are not required to provide prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and publication tariffs; approximately CHF 600-900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate, identity, good-standing and authorization documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin or Swiss consulate for non-apostille states

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translation office recognized by the cantonal court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of CHF 0.45-0.70 per line or CHF 120-220 per certified page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, AML/CFT due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary or practicing attorney engaged as compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for medium-risk enhanced due diligence under AMLA and FINMA requirements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and administrative domicile setup, including first-year address provision at a licensed fiduciary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary / administrative domicile provider in the canton of registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CHF 1,200-2,000 for the first year, including commercial substance support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory pre-clearance and legal opinion on ocean freight forwarding / NVOCC licensing, customs intermediation and corporate governance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss external legal counsel with freight forwarding and commercial register expertise
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a scope-limited legal opinion and regulatory pre-clearance memorandum

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Arts. 629, 633, 634, 640, 716a, 716b; Swiss Register of Commerce Ordinance (HRegV), Arts. 32-42; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRegG).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA) via the Cantonal Commercial Register of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Gründungsanzeige / Déclaration de fondation (Declaration of Formation) filed for entry in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000 for an AG, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash at incorporation; funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank. In-kind contributions require a licensed auditor's (Revisionsstelle) report confirming full value; bearer shares are abolished.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The incorporation subscription list dated [____] is ratified; the subscribers' contributions totaling CHF 100,000 are acknowledged as paid up to the statutory minimum of CHF 50,000 into the blocked escrow account; 2. The registered office of the company is hereby fixed at [Street, Zug, Switzerland]; 3. The following persons are appointed as officers: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chair of the Board of Directors, each with sole/collective signatory authority; 4. The Board delegates operational management to the CEO; 5. The Company initiates NVOCC/ocean freight forwarding licensing proceedings; 6. All further acts to perfect registration are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Founding Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Zug notary to authenticate the articles of association (Statuten), the founding report (Gründungsbericht), and the subscription list. Verify that the corporate purpose expressly includes international freight forwarding, NVOCC ocean container brokerage, and logistics agency services. Execute all signatures in the presence of the notary; the notary will transmit the application to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founders and board members
Notarized power of attorney for formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the documents, instruct the notary to file a corrective declaration within 10 days; amend inconsistencies and re-notarize revised clauses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss Bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS Switzerland, or Julius Bär)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-operative corporate escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the company's future name; deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the minimum capital; obtain a bank blocking certificate (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) confirming the deposit, the blocking conditions, and the authorized withdrawing signatories.
required_dossiers: Formation draft of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account, select an alternate licensed bank or convert the contribution to an in-kind asset with an auditor's valuation certificate; re-open the account and issue a new blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Declaration of Formation with supporting resolutions via the Swiss commercial register electronic portal (the cantonal office processes through the system linked to the Swiss Federal Commercial Register). Include the board members' declarations of consent, the auditor's appointment (unless an opt-out applies for small companies by unanimous shareholder consent), and the precise share capital division. Upon approval, the registry assigns the company its Swiss UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer).
required_dossiers: Consent declarations of all board directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry issues a formal query (Verfügung) requesting clarifications; reply within 10 calendar days with amended instruments; if registration is refused, appeal to the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Publication and Identity Release
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Feuille officielle suisse du commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the Commercial Register office automatically transmits the company particulars to the SHAB for official publication. Verify the published entry for accuracy of name, domicile, business purpose, share capital, and signatory powers; obtain the definitive UID number and register extract (Handelsregisterauszug).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains errors, file an immediate correction request with the Commercial Register office; a rectified publication will be issued at no court cost if the error is administrative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax, Social Insurance, and Statutory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA); Cantonal Tax Administration Zug; Zug Social Insurance Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for corporate income tax (obligatory upon Commercial Register entry), apply for VAT number (MWST) if taxable turnover threshold is met or voluntarily, and register employees with the social insurance compensation scheme (AHV/IV/EO). For NVOCC activities, subscribe to customs turnover tax and, if applicable, apply for an excise duty permit for bonded goods handling.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority issues an extended information request, respond with the corporate register extract, bank certificate, and sworn declarations; appeal any denial of the VAT number to the Federal Tax Court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the AG; Corporate bank of choice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Board, adopt internal organizational regulations (Organisationsreglement), issue definitive share certificates, maintain the share register, disclose ultimate beneficial owners for AML purposes, and release the blocked capital by presenting the Commercial Register entry to the bank. Open the operational business account for freight settlement (SWIFT/WIRE and ACH rails as needed).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account activation, resubmit the register extract and board resolution with certified translations; escalate within the bank's legal compliance department or switch to a second licensed bank using the same formation dossier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Federal Office of Transport (BAV) in coordination with the Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS); additionally, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for commercial freight brokerage conduct rules
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Freight Forwarding Operating Permit / Gütertransportvermittler-Bewilligung (NVOCC and Ocean Freight Forwarding License) under the Swiss Ordinance on Goods Transport Agencies, together with a customs transit tr/t/Customs Broker authorization for third-party customs filings

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and Cantonal Environmental Office Zug (Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration (low-tier) — Full EIA report not required for administrative office-based NVOCC brokerage; mandatory registration applies if the company operates container deconsolidation, warehousing, or cold storage facilities exceeding 1,500 m² or handling dangerous goods.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for industrial wastewater; Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV) limiting total VOC emissions to 20 mg/m³ at exhaust discharge; Ordinance on the Movements of Waste (VEVA) and OECD hazardous waste rules for cargo residue handling; noise limits per the Swiss Noise Abatement Ordinance (LSV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Cantonal Fire Insurance Office of Zug (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) confirming fire load calculation, escape routes, and hydrant spacing; Structural load inspection certificate for the registered office premises; Occupational clearance under Arts. 82-84 of the Swiss Labor Act (ArbG) confirming workstation ergonomics, ventilation, electrical safety (niederspannungsverordnung), and first-aid equipment, delivered by SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Association).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), VAT Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer), Eigerstrasse 65, 3003 Bern, Switzerland. Tax registration/e-filing portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT returns and registrations are handled through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's 'SuisseTax' e-services platform and the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss-resident Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) after notarial incorporation, the company is registered with the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister), and the Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the statutory business identifier (UID / IDE / IDI) in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX; (2) the cantonal tax administration registers the AG for direct federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax; (3) VAT registration is a separate obligation: the AG must apply to the ESTV VAT Division using the official Swiss VAT registration form—supported by the articles of association, the UID/commercial register extract, a shareholder register, and, for non-resident founders, a proof of foreign tax residency—when annual worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; the ESTV then issues the VAT number consisting of the UID plus the suffix 'MWST' (e.g., CHE-116.430.123 MWST) and the corresponding S/M (taxpayer) reference; (4) registration must be filed within 30 days of the day the obligation arises under Art. 73 of the Swiss VAT Act (MWSTG). For a non-resident foreign entity without a Swiss seat or permanent establishment: the entity must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (domiciliary) unless the FTA waives the requirement on the basis of an administrative-assistance arrangement; registration is made through the same ESTV procedure, the foreign entity receives a Swiss VAT number, and, where no Swiss VAT registration is required but Swiss input VAT is incurred, the foreign enterprise may use the separate FTA VAT-refund procedure (refund for foreign companies). A freight-forwarding licence under Swiss legislation (e.g., the Freight Forwarding Ordinance) is additionally required for the NVOCC activity, but it is not a precondition for the VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Swiss AG is a capital company with separate legal personality: it cannot be treated as a pass-through and is taxed at entity level. For direct taxes, a Swiss-resident AG has unlimited tax liability for its worldwide income and net assets (subject to participation relief, international tax treaties and the Swiss corporate tax reform STAF framework); it is subject to Swiss federal income tax of 8.5% on net profit after payment of tax (prefederal-effective rate of 4.26%) plus cantonal/communal corporate income tax and annual capital tax (cantonal variation; e.g., Zug). For Swiss VAT purposes, the AG is a 'taxable person' under Art. 10 MWSTG with entity-level Swiss VAT obligations for supplies of goods and services made in Switzerland. There is no statutory pass-through election for the AG, and no territorial-zone or general tax-exempt-zone regime applies in Switzerland (with narrowly limited exceptions such as customs free zones only for customs law).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election or a hybrid-mismatch classification declaration; the legal form governs tax classification. Available elections relevant to the AG are: (i) VAT exemption for small businesses under Art. 11 MWSTG, with an irrevocable election (option) to waive the exemption and become ordinarily taxable, usable when annual worldwide turnover does not exceed CHF 100,000; (ii) VAT group taxation (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) under Art. 15 MWSTG, allowing a controlling parent and its subsidiaries to be treated as one taxable person for VAT if the parent directly or indirectly holds a majority of voting/quota rights and the group's total turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; (iii) direct federal corporate income-tax group (Steuergruppe) under Art. 60 DBG, effective from 2021, which allows a parent and its Swiss subsidiaries (at least 50% direct/indirect participation in capital and voting rights) to offset profits and losses within the group on an elective basis; (iv) Swiss participation relief (Schachtelprivileg) applying automatically to qualifying dividends and capital gains on participations of at least 10% (or with a market value above CHF 1 million) held for at least 12 months; and (v) deemed-liquidation options for migration/hybrid-transfers under the MLLI/OECD framework, which require a formal application to the competent tax administration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer/MwSt, TVA, IVA), governed by the Federal Act of 12 June 2009 on Value Added Tax (SR 641.20) and the VAT Ordinance (SR 641.201). Switzerland is not an EU VAT member state, so the Swiss VAT system is a separate non-harmonised federal turnover tax; there is no separate GST or state-level sales tax, and no customs-union intra-EU regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 para 2 lit. a MWSTG). The threshold applies to Swiss-resident businesses; a non-resident business is also required to register for Swiss VAT when it performs supplies taxable in Switzerland in excess of CHF 100,000 in a Swiss assessment period, except for supplies on which the Swiss customer is already liable under reverse-charge rules. Below the threshold the AG may freely elect VAT liability (small-business option under Art. 11 MWSTG).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has not implemented a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital-stamping system (no Italian-style SdI, no SaA-style B2B clearance). The ESTV requires tax-registered companies to submit VAT returns electronically via the 'SuisseTax' e-services portal; mandatory invoice content corresponds to Art. 26a MWSTG (supplier name and address, Swiss VAT number, buyer's name/address, type of supply, date, consideration, VAT rate and VAT amount). For payment purposes, the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is the standard and is mandatory for all pay-in slips issued after 30 June 2020 to Swiss payment service providers; e-invoicing on the Peppol/eBill rails is voluntary, not tax-cleared. Customs declarations (including export declarations) are filed electronically through the Swiss single-window system 'e-dec' and, for transit, the NCTS. A VAT-charge and input-VAT ledger must be kept in an auditable form (Art. 70 MWSTG) and made available to the FTA on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and certain cross-border services are eligible for the 0% VAT rate under Art. 23 para 2 MWSTG and Art. 52 of the Swiss VAT Ordinance. For the NVOCC/ocean freight-forwarding AG, eligibility covers: (a) supply of goods exported from the Swiss customs territory or into a customs free zone/receptacle, provided the goods are physically transported abroad and the supplier proves the export by an official customs document; (b) services directly connected with the import, export or transit of goods, including maritime and air cargo transport, ocean freight forwarding and NVOCC box brokerage, port/handling/stevedoring charges, container detention/leasing during the international carriage, warehousing of goods in transit, and any services that the Swiss Austrian-style zero-rating provisions treat as incidental to international transport; (c) services supplied to non-Swiss recipients whose place of supply is abroad pursuant to Art. 8 MWSTG (in which case the supply is outside the Swiss VAT net; if such services have a sufficiently close nexus to Switzerland, they may instead be zero-rated). The zero-rating is conditional on the supplier keeping contemporaneous evidence proving that the goods actually left Switzerland or that the service is used abroad; for freight-forwarding services, a booking-contract reference to export/import consignments, the ocean carrier's bill of lading, and customs exit proofs must be retained. Input VAT incurred on Swiss costs attributable to zero-rated export revenue is creditable, and the AG may obtain a refund/credit through the normal VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Official Customs Export Declaration / Ausfuhranmeldung prepared through the Swiss 'e-dec' electronic customs system, including the customs-issued movement/exit reference confirming departure from Swiss customs territory

Bill of Lading (original or electronic; for NVOCCs also the house bill of lading and a sea waybill/master bill of lading issued by the underlying carrier) showing the foreign port of discharge and the consignee abroad

Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit note (e.g., SWIFT MT103 or an ACH/SWIFT bank statement) evidencing the receipt of export/foreign-currency proceeds from the foreign buyer in the NVOCC AG's Swiss bank account
Commercial invoice, package list and the freight-forwarding/booking contract (contract of carriage, instruction from the shipper/consignee) with Incoterms identifying the international destination
Supporting transport and customs-trail documents: CMR road consignment note, rail waybill, air waybill, terminal/container yard receipts, port inbound/outbound manifests and transshipment evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss law imposes no statutory exchange-control or explicit 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline (Switzerland has no exchange controls); the 180-day window is followed by exporters and used by the FTA as a commercial-regularity benchmark in transfer-pricing and transaction-integrity checks. The ESTV conducts field VAT audits (normally every 2-4 years; frequency increases with export-heavy business models, NVOCC structures and banking anti-money-laundering risk profiles) and verifies export declarations, shipping files, bills of lading, original transport documents and bank inflow statements. Where the zero-rating is not substantiated or the goods/Swiss-attributable services are found to have been consumed or delivered in Switzerland, the FTA retrospectively re-characterises the supplies as taxable at the domestic rate (8.1% for the period from 1 January 2024; 7.7% for earlier periods), denies the related input VAT deductions, and issues a clawback assessment for the underdeclared VAT, plus statutory default interest from the due date of each affected period. Under Art. 96 MWSTG, intentional tax evasion (including deliberate or seriously negligent misuse of export zero-rating and false export evidence) attracts a penalty up to three times the evaded tax; aggravating cases may be prosecuted as criminal VAT fraud under Art. 97 MWSTG with monetary penalties up to CHF 250,000 and imprisonment up to two years. Negligent procedural violations are subject to summary fines under Art. 97 para 2 MWSTG (generally up to CHF 10,000, and up to CHF 100,000 in serious cases). The clawback period for retrospective assessment is ten years after the end of the fiscal year in which the tax liability arose, and Swiss criminal-tax limitation is fifteen years for aggravated fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), Schwarztorstrasse 41, 3003 Bern, acting under the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment (WZG, 2000) and in coordination with FINMA for banking supervision; the State Secretariat for International Financial Affairs (SIF) handles international financial policy, while the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) administers Swiss economic sanctions and embargo measures that condition cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current account and capital account. Switzerland maintains no general exchange control legislation, no surrender or conversion mandates for export earnings, and no restriction on the repatriation of dividends, shareholder loan repayments, sales proceeds, or liquidation balances. The only material profit-remittance hurdle is tax-related: an ordinary 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends, which is fully refundable or exonerated if the shareholder qualifies for participation relief (10% holding or market value of at least CHF 1 million) or if a double tax treaty reduces the residual rate. For a freight-forwarding NVOCC structured as a Swiss AG, overseas shareholder remittances are therefore operationally unrestricted but should be documented with minutes of the board of directors and audited financial statements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The Swiss National Bank does not impose any mandatory timeline or percentage for the surrender of export proceeds. Ocean freight receipts denominated in USD, EUR, or other foreign currencies may be accumulated in correspondent accounts abroad, retained in multi-currency Swiss bank accounts, converted to CHF at freely negotiated interbank rates, or hedged using permissible FX derivatives. There is also no obligation to repatriate export documentation for central bank statistical purposes other than general reporting requirements that apply to Swiss resident banks, not to the exporting corporate itself.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Einlagekonto) and Operational Multi-Currency Corporate Account in CHF/USD/EUR
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account with Treasury eBanking and SWIFT connectivity
Operational Corporate Account and Trade Finance Facility (CHF/EUR/USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV, Avenu de la Gare 10, 1003 Lausanne)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account with Documentary Credit and Cargo Receivables Discounting Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium viability for offshore digital EMIs. Switzerland has no direct EMIs licence; only banks, FINMA-licensed fintech institutions (limited to CHF 100 million public deposits), or clients of a licensed payment services provider under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA) can legally hold Swiss client money. An offshore UK FCA EMI or EU-regulated EMI may not open a domestic Swiss payment account or accept deposits from the Swiss resident CH_AG as a core service. Cross-border use is possible only in a narrow, ancillary gate for third-country freight counterparties, and the AG must still maintain a fully compliant Swiss bank settlement account to channel final clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorised director or a senior officer with confirmed signature power must ordinarily appear physically for the account-opening interview when the entity is a new Swiss AG with non-resident ownership and an enhanced due diligence business class such as an NVOCC. Remote opening via FINMA-compliant video identification may be accepted by selected banks if the director has already been identified by a Swiss notary and the corporate KYC document pack is submitted through an existing private banker or legal counsel, but the underwriting committee retains discretion to require a personal meeting in Zurich, Geneva, Zug, or Lausanne.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed third-party freight settlors; consolidated wire transfers for shipments benefitting multiple unrelated cargo owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial file for each consolidated shipment: signed NVOCC contract, master and house bills of lading, freight invoices issued by CH_AG to each customer, SWIFT field 70 payment references, updated UBO register extract, and an AML questionnaire explaining the settlement chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure from port calls, flag-of-convenience vessels, or cargoes destined to/from SECO-, OFAC- or UN-sanctioned territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level automated Denied Party Screening (DPS) logs, vessel AIS transit records, full bill-of-lading and container-tracking history, SECO embargo screening evidence, and contractual obligations binding charterers/customers to sanctions compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-revenue freight forwarding with low Swiss capitalisation or unexpected cash sweeps between related foreign entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited Swiss financial statements, treasury cash-flow forecast, formal intercompany services agreement, transfer pricing file in accordance with the Swiss and OECD TP rules, and notarized board minutes approving each treasury movement between CH_AG and related parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags, including invoice values inconsistent with goods descriptions, over/under-invoicing, or duplicate settlement of ocean freight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundled invoice, packing list, verified gross mass (VGM) certificate, container number/tamper-seal evidence, customs declarations in the National Customs System (NCTS), and, where discrepancies existed, a signed corrected bill of lading and written explanation to the bank's AML investigation team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal trading accounts or offshore shell entities as the ORIGINATOR/beneficiary of freight settlement payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group corporate chart showing direct ownership of CH_AG, a notarized AML beneficial-owner declaration, evidence that every freight settlement account is held in the AG's name, and an executive-level attestation from an external auditor confirming the alignment of account numbers and counterparty contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial AG capitalization and subsequent shareholder capital infusions, the compliant routing is a wire transfer via SWIFT MT103 (or SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent-bank-transmitted funds) referencing in field 70: 'Subscribed capital contribution / Einlage auf Kernkapital - Freigabe per notarieller Urkunde dated [date]'. The receiving Swiss clearing bank executes the credit through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) or its equivalent EUR/USD correspondent chain (e.g., SIG, EURO1/CHATS). The bank will require release confirmation from the notary, the notarial deed of incorporation, board minutes, and an escrow-release instruction from the existing capital escrow account. Foreign currency must be converted at the bank's prevailing exchange rate unless the account is maintained as a multi-currency treasury account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the NVOCC freight forwarder, settlement should run through: (1) SWIFT MT103 for ocean freight brokerage settlements, port disbursement accounts, customs agents, and inland hauliers; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank treasury rebalancing or large cross-credit repositioning between the CHF, USD and EUR accounts of the AG; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC at sight or short-tenor usance) for high-value cargo-chartering and terminal service contracts where the beneficiary requires documentary protection; and (4) SEPA Credit Transfer for Eurozone port, rail, and road-freight receivables and disbursements. Where necessary, urgent high-value payments may be sent through Target2-SECB or a Swiss SIC instant payment endpoint, but the corporate-treasury default rail remains serial MT103 to preserve auditability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot and outright deliverable forward contracts between CHF and EUR/USD/GBP
Deliverable forward contracts for liquid currencies of main corridor markets (EUR, USD, GBP)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or non-convertible corridor currencies used in NVOCC transit routes where physical CHF settlement is prohibited or illiquid
Cross-currency swaps (CKS) between USD and CHF or USD and EUR for multi-year charter or terminal cash-flow matching
Currency options (options on forwards and structured FX forwards) executed with a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex (CSA) governed by Swiss law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) and competent Cantonal Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year end, normally 30 June for calendar year; extension possible upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a. on arrears; administrative fines up to one-third of tax evaded; default assessment if no return filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax (VAT) Return (Swiss VAT declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after end of each VAT reporting period (quarterly, or annually if turnover below CHF 5 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-interest at 5% p.a.; late filing penalty up to CHF 5,000; simple tax evasion fine up to three times the tax due

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) Minutes and Approved Financial Statements (retained in minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public filing for small companies (audit exemption); commercial register filing only if statutory audit obliged or listed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors jointly liable for default; statutory penalty up to CHF 200,000 for breach of disclosure duties; private enforcement by shareholders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO) Update and Confirmatory Note in Case of Share Transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal register; accessible to legally entitled authorities (AML supervisory bodies and law enforcement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately upon any change; no annual default filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to CHF 200,000 for false or omitted entry; administrative enforcement and deregistration risk for persistent violation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Change Notifications (Directors, Share Capital, Registered Office) and any necessary Administrative Renewals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven; no annual blank filing. For a calendar-year entity, not a standing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration fines for late filing (administrative penalty up to CHF 5,000); continued noncompliance may trigger official strike-off or dissolution pursuant to Art. 935 CO

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required when any two of three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive years: balance sheet total > CHF 20 million; annual revenue > CHF 40 million; average full-time employees > 250. Small companies with balance sheet total < CHF 10 million, revenue < CHF 20 million and fewer than 50 employees may waive audit by unanimous shareholder resolution. All other companies require a limited audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 958–963); IFRS permitted for listed groups and voluntary adoptable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland has no annual UBO declaration filing. A current register of beneficial owners must be maintained at all times. Share transfers trigger an immediate update to the register showing the new beneficial owner's identity and economic interest. Non-compliance constitutes a criminal offense under the Criminal Code and the Anti-Money Laundering Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Annual General Meeting and Board Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 5,000 – 20,000 (ca. USD 5,500 – 22,000) for limited or ordinary audit depending on company size

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on profit after federal tax; combined federal, cantonal and communal headline rate for a Zug Aktiengesellschaft is approximately 11.9%-12.4%, with high-tax cantons reaching up to approximately 21.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Switzerland. Preferential mechanisms include the participation deduction for substantial dividend and capital-gain income, R&D super-deduction and patent-box relief in most cantons, notional interest deduction in adopting cantons, and tax-neutral restructuring relief. An operating Zug freight-forwarding/NVOCC entity will normally incur an aggregate effective Swiss tax burden of roughly 11.9%-12.4% before applicable deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss combined cantonal/federal corporate income tax return: 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' / 'Déclaration fiscale personnes morales' filed through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) eTax portal and the Zug cantonal tax e-filing platform. The federal withholding tax return and VAT return are filed separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, accompanied by quarterly provisional profit tax instalments based on the most recent assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate tax return is due within six months after the close of the business year; for a 31 December year-end this is normally 30 June of the following year. A written extension may be available up to twelve months. Quarterly prepayments are typically due 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register the exact legal entity name, legal form 'Aktiengesellschaft', registered office, CHE-UID number, ISIC/NAICS business scope and the Swiss NVOCC/freight forwarding licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parents and ultimate beneficial owners must be disclosed; failure to identify the foreign parent may trigger AML, tax disclosure and treaty-benefit denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State share capital, statutory legal reserves, capital contribution reserves and retained earnings. This section is used for capital tax and thin-capitalisation assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany shareholder debt must be documented and bear arm's length interest; excess debt can be reclassified as equity and interest deductions denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross ocean freight, NVOCC consolidation fees, brokerage commissions and ancillary revenues; deduct vessel costs, port charges, container handling, third-party haulage, insurance, wages, rent and depreciation; make mandatory tax add-backs such as unnecessary business expenses and non-arm's length management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All charges invoiced by non-resident affiliates must be supported by contracts, invoices, proof of actual service and functional/risk documentation; otherwise the Swiss entity is required to make an add-back for hidden profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Deductions, Losses and Participation Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the seven-year loss carry-forward utilisation, participation deductions on qualifying substantial shareholdings, R&D deductions, patent-box amounts and any cantonal investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation relief is only available if the Swiss AG holds at least 10% of the nominal share capital or has a qualifying market value participation; foreign shareholding evidence must accompany the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Withholding Tax Statement / Dividend Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all distributions, constructive benefits, cash dividends, interest and royalties paid to related parties, including the gross amount and applicable Swiss withholding tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident dividend recipients must be identified by jurisdiction; the statutory 35% Verrechnungssteuer must be declared unless a valid DTA relief-at-source approval or refund claim is in place.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing leads to forced assessment, procedural fines up to CHF 10,000, default interest and potential tax evasion penalties. Simple tax evasion carries a fine up to the amount of evaded tax; deliberate tax fraud with forged documents carries a fine up to three times the evaded federal tax and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax on gross dividends paid by a Swiss AG; treaty-resident shareholders may obtain a reduced rate of 5%-15%, and 0%-5% for qualifying substantial direct holdings under many Swiss DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home tax authority and submit it together with a Swiss withholding tax relief/refund application to ESTV. The application must include a beneficial ownership statement, shareholding evidence and the relevant DTA article. Unless a relief-at-source agreement has been pre-approved, the Swiss paying agent must withhold the full 35% and the foreign shareholder must reclaim the withheld amount within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became distributable. Relief is denied where the ultimate owner lacks substance, is not treaty-resident, or fails the anti-abuse/beneficial ownership test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Swiss AG to a non-resident licensor are not subject to Swiss withholding tax; they become taxable in Switzerland only if the foreign recipient carries on business through a Swiss permanent establishment. Interest on bank deposits, bonds, money market instruments and publicly offered debenture loans is subject to the statutory 35% withholding tax; ordinary intercompany trade credit and direct corporate loans are generally outside the Swiss WHT net. Treaty rates under most Swiss DTAs range from 0%-10% for interest and 0%-10% for royalties, subject to the same TRC and beneficial-ownership relief procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland applies an SME safe-harbour: full OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation is not automatically demanded where the Swiss entity has fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover below CHF 20 million. Above this threshold, a contemporaneous Local File must be available upon cantonal or federal demand; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report become expected where the worldwide group consolidated turnover exceeds CHF 900 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a Guernsey-style ESR, but the Swiss tax system requires real economic substance through the 'place of effective management' concept and the principle of a genuine commercial AB. A Zug NVOCC/ocean freight forwarder must maintain a physical office, locally resident managers or employees, board meetings in Switzerland, complete cargo and booking records, bank accounts and actual operational control of container consolidation and freight negotiations. A letter-box company is disregarded for tax purposes, profits may be allocated to the foreign controlling principal and treaty benefits may be denied under anti-abuse rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Forged Shipping and Accounting Documents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting freight revenue, using fabricated bills of lading, booking fictitious container costs, double-declaring stevedoring charges, or engaging shell suppliers to manufacture deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment with default interest plus a fine equal to the evaded tax for simple evasion; for tax fraud involving forged documents, a fine up to three times the evaded federal tax and imprisonment may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or order document falsification are jointly and severally liable under Article 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, subject to criminal fines, imprisonment up to three years, and pretrial travel bans in aggravated cases.
